text: Envy is a worm that gnaws and consumes the entrails of the envious.
source: Sayings of the Ynca Pachacutec (Garcilaso de la Vega, Royal Commentaries, Bk 6)
era: Inca ruler of the 15th c. CE; recorded c. 1609

text: He that envies and is envied, has a double torment.
source: Sayings of the Ynca Pachacutec (Garcilaso de la Vega, Royal Commentaries, Bk 6)
era: Inca ruler of the 15th c. CE; recorded c. 1609

text: He that envies another, injures himself.
source: Sayings of the Ynca Pachacutec (Garcilaso de la Vega, Royal Commentaries, Bk 6)
era: Inca ruler of the 15th c. CE; recorded c. 1609

text: It is better that others should envy you for being good, than that you should envy others, you yourself being evil.
source: Sayings of the Ynca Pachacutec (Garcilaso de la Vega, Royal Commentaries, Bk 6)
era: Inca ruler of the 15th c. CE; recorded c. 1609

text: He that kills another without authority or just cause, condemns himself to death.
source: Sayings of the Ynca Pachacutec (Garcilaso de la Vega, Royal Commentaries, Bk 6)
era: Inca ruler of the 15th c. CE; recorded c. 1609

text: The noble and generous man is known by the patience he shows in adversity.
source: Sayings of the Ynca Pachacutec (Garcilaso de la Vega, Royal Commentaries, Bk 6)
era: Inca ruler of the 15th c. CE; recorded c. 1609

text: Impatience is the sign of a vile and base mind, badly taught and worse accustomed.
source: Sayings of the Ynca Pachacutec (Garcilaso de la Vega, Royal Commentaries, Bk 6)
era: Inca ruler of the 15th c. CE; recorded c. 1609

text: The man who knows not how to govern his house and family, will know much less how to rule a state.
source: Sayings of the Ynca Pachacutec (Garcilaso de la Vega, Royal Commentaries, Bk 6)
era: Inca ruler of the 15th c. CE; recorded c. 1609
